files.Versi n Completa _El teatro y la cultura:
1
00:00:21,708 --> 00:00:24,083
How are we doing?
Nice to see you here.

2
00:00:24,167 --> 00:00:26,958
It's a pleasure to be with you.

3
00:00:28,083 --> 00:00:31,292
I'm a little nervous, I'm
telling you now so you know.

4
00:00:31,375 --> 00:00:35,458
I would love for us to spend
some quality time together chatting.  I

5
00:00:35,542 --> 00:00:38,625
don't know if what I have to tell you will
interest you,

6
00:00:38,708 --> 00:00:40,000
but I'll try.

7
00:00:41,042 --> 00:00:43,083
My name is Blanca Portillo,

8
00:00:43,167 --> 00:00:45,375
I am also known
as Rojiblanca Portillo.

9
00:00:46,500 --> 00:00:49,875
I have been with Atlético de Madrid
all my life.  I

10
00:00:50,375 --> 00:00:53,292
declare myself addicted to acting.

11
00:00:53,750 --> 00:00:56,250
It's what I love most in the world

12
00:00:56,917 --> 00:01:01,667
and what I dedicate all my time,
energy and passion to.

13
00:01:03,042 --> 00:01:06,208
I would love to share with you
how I got started in this

14
00:01:06,292 --> 00:01:08,083
and why I love it the way I do.

15
00:01:09,042 --> 00:01:10,875
First of all, it changed my life.

16
00:01:10,958 --> 00:01:13,750
Secondly,
it is what has taught me the most

17
00:01:14,333 --> 00:01:16,917
in all the experiences I have had.  It has

18
00:01:17,000 --> 00:01:20,333
been my guide,
what has opened the doors to the world for me,

19
00:01:20,417 --> 00:01:23,042
what has made me
know myself

20
00:01:23,125 --> 00:01:24,542
and others better.

21
00:01:24,625 --> 00:01:27,125
I am the fourth daughter of eight.

22
00:01:27,667 --> 00:01:31,375
We are eight siblings
from a very normal family.

23
00:01:32,250 --> 00:01:36,125
Rather pulling towards a low economy.

24
00:01:37,167 --> 00:01:39,917
My father died
when I was 18 years old.

25
00:01:41,958 --> 00:01:45,208
I studied vocational training
when I finished high school.

26
00:01:45,292 --> 00:01:46,792
What used to be the EGB.

27
00:01:47,583 --> 00:01:50,583
And I studied
professional administration training.

28
00:01:51,167 --> 00:01:53,542
When I was 13 or 14 years old I

29
00:01:53,625 --> 00:01:56,083
didn't really know
what I wanted to be in life, I

30
00:01:56,167 --> 00:01:58,125
didn't have the slightest idea.

31
00:01:58,208 --> 00:02:01,458
I loved the idea
of telling stories,

32
00:02:02,042 --> 00:02:05,833
because I admit that I have been a reader
since I was very little.

33
00:02:07,375 --> 00:02:08,458
Because, probably,

34
00:02:08,542 --> 00:02:10,542
since I didn't like the life I had,

35
00:02:11,625 --> 00:02:14,458
the best way to escape it
was by reading.  I

36
00:02:15,750 --> 00:02:18,625
put myself inside a book
and lived that book, I

37
00:02:18,708 --> 00:02:20,417
lived as the characters lived

38
00:02:20,500 --> 00:02:23,708
and I was transported to other places,
to other worlds,

39
00:02:23,792 --> 00:02:26,375
to other cities, to other paradises.

40
00:02:26,458 --> 00:02:30,167
This allowed me to escape a reality that,
let me tell you, I didn't like very much.

41
00:02:31,750 --> 00:02:33,417
After studying the training,

42
00:02:33,500 --> 00:02:37,042
I decided
that if I wanted to tell stories

43
00:02:37,125 --> 00:02:40,292
or contact people,
which I really liked too,

44
00:02:41,708 --> 00:02:44,625
the best profession I could choose,
don't laugh,

45
00:02:45,417 --> 00:02:48,375
was a conference hostess.
Why?  Well, I don't know.

46
00:02:48,958 --> 00:02:53,042
I thought it was interesting to be with people, to
be able to share

47
00:02:53,125 --> 00:02:56,000
and, if I had a conference, I would
surely learn things

48
00:02:56,083 --> 00:02:59,583
and could, well,
grow in a certain way.

49
00:03:00,000 --> 00:03:02,292
I started studying this.

50
00:03:04,042 --> 00:03:06,208
I went to a few conferences

51
00:03:06,292 --> 00:03:08,292
where I was bored to death.

52
00:03:09,167 --> 00:03:11,208
They put a uniform on you and you just had to

53
00:03:11,292 --> 00:03:14,625
say good afternoon, come by,
good afternoon, come by...

54
00:03:14,708 --> 00:03:17,833
And that wasn't telling stories
or being with people.

55
00:03:17,917 --> 00:03:20,167
But I was lucky
to have a teacher,

56
00:03:20,792 --> 00:03:23,500
a teacher
who taught us Tourist Geography.

57
00:03:24,292 --> 00:03:28,042
And he had a theater group.

58
00:03:28,750 --> 00:03:31,417
I had no connection with the theater.

59
00:03:31,500 --> 00:03:34,375
In my personal life...
My mother and grandmother

60
00:03:34,458 --> 00:03:37,375
liked going to the theater and the cinema,

61
00:03:38,417 --> 00:03:41,083
but I had only been there
once in my life.

62
00:03:41,958 --> 00:03:43,208
No more.

63
00:03:43,292 --> 00:03:45,333
I fell in love with that teacher.

64
00:03:45,417 --> 00:03:48,208
Everything he explained was so fascinating, he

65
00:03:48,292 --> 00:03:50,125
was so intelligent, so wonderful... It

66
00:03:50,208 --> 00:03:51,958
was a very platonic love.

67
00:03:52,833 --> 00:03:57,375
Sitting and listening to him
was like reading a book,

68
00:03:57,458 --> 00:03:58,625
traveling to other places.

69
00:03:58,708 --> 00:04:01,875
It opened your mind, made you analyze
things in a different way.

70
00:04:02,250 --> 00:04:06,208
At that time, he was choosing people

71
00:04:06,917 --> 00:04:09,292
to join his theater group,

72
00:04:09,375 --> 00:04:12,833
who were somewhat select,
the group of the exquisite.  I did

73
00:04:13,500 --> 00:04:15,125
n't get in the first year,

74
00:04:15,208 --> 00:04:20,083
and in the second year he invited me
to participate in the theater group.

75
00:04:21,167 --> 00:04:24,667
At that time,
I was very obsessed with Lorca.  I've

76
00:04:25,792 --> 00:04:27,667
always liked him, since I was young,

77
00:04:27,750 --> 00:04:30,833
and the whole story around him,
everything that happened to him.

78
00:04:31,417 --> 00:04:35,333
This moment in Spanish history
fascinated me.

79
00:04:35,417 --> 00:04:39,208
Such a wonderful poet that
we suddenly lost in such a strange way.

80
00:04:40,417 --> 00:04:43,708
And he was making a play about Lorca,
curiously enough.

81
00:04:44,458 --> 00:04:46,917
Then,
to be able to be in that group, I said:

82
00:04:47,000 --> 00:04:48,250
“Let's be there.”

83
00:04:49,417 --> 00:04:53,417
I had a boyfriend
who I was going to marry.  We

84
00:04:54,417 --> 00:04:55,917
already had an apartment,

85
00:04:56,000 --> 00:04:58,208
we had a lot of things
more or less done.

86
00:04:58,292 --> 00:05:02,167
I was 18 years old, I was very young,
but I was very clear

87
00:05:02,250 --> 00:05:04,625
that he was, in a way,
the man of my life

88
00:05:05,292 --> 00:05:08,542
and that, on the other hand, there was
my profession or my career.

89
00:05:08,625 --> 00:05:10,875
Then,
when we started doing theater,

90
00:05:11,750 --> 00:05:14,042
I discovered a

91
00:05:14,667 --> 00:05:16,875
completely strange world

92
00:05:18,083 --> 00:05:21,375
that made me travel for real, not by reading.

93
00:05:21,958 --> 00:05:25,833
The character was me
and the one experiencing things was me.

94
00:05:26,708 --> 00:05:30,083
One day at a rehearsal,
someone who was watching this rehearsal

95
00:05:30,167 --> 00:05:34,042
approached me and said,
“You really moved me.”

96
00:05:35,458 --> 00:05:38,500
And that became the pinnacle,

97
00:05:38,583 --> 00:05:43,250
thinking that the emotion
I felt while doing that work,

98
00:05:43,750 --> 00:05:46,458
or that research,
because it wasn't even a job,

99
00:05:47,250 --> 00:05:49,667
transcended my own being

100
00:05:49,750 --> 00:05:53,875
and connected with another who was
in front of me and produced an emotion in him.

101
00:05:54,542 --> 00:05:58,375
That was like saying:
"It can't be, this is magic.

102
00:05:58,792 --> 00:06:02,625
In other words, what I feel,
someone outside can feel,

103
00:06:02,708 --> 00:06:06,125
saying things and experiencing things,
not reading them."

104
00:06:06,958 --> 00:06:10,958
From that moment on, I decided
that that was what I wanted to do.  It

105
00:06:12,125 --> 00:06:15,375
combined the two things
that interested me most,

106
00:06:15,458 --> 00:06:17,708
which was telling stories

107
00:06:19,083 --> 00:06:20,625
and being with people,

108
00:06:20,708 --> 00:06:25,125
because a large part of this work
is related to the idea of teamwork.

109
00:06:26,292 --> 00:06:28,708
Interpretation does
not exist by itself,

110
00:06:28,792 --> 00:06:29,833
you with yourself,

111
00:06:29,917 --> 00:06:32,000
but there must be a receiver

112
00:06:32,083 --> 00:06:34,250
and, then,
people with whom you share it.

113
00:06:35,583 --> 00:06:39,167
I remember that I didn't know
that this was being studied.

114
00:06:40,292 --> 00:06:44,208
Then, the boyfriend I had told me:
“Well, yes, there is a place called the

115
00:06:44,292 --> 00:06:47,542
Real Escuela Superior
de Arte Dramático y Danza de Madrid”.

116
00:06:48,375 --> 00:06:50,167
"And what is studied there?"

117
00:06:50,625 --> 00:06:52,750
"Let's go see it."  I approached it.

118
00:06:52,833 --> 00:06:56,333
At that time it was in the Plaza de Ópera,
where the Teatro Real is today.

119
00:06:57,125 --> 00:06:58,417
I took some tests

120
00:06:58,500 --> 00:07:02,125
where they asked you to
interpret a text in verse

121
00:07:02,917 --> 00:07:05,792
and do an improvisation
and a written exam.  They took

122
00:07:06,500 --> 00:07:10,042
me, I passed.

123
00:07:10,750 --> 00:07:12,667
And then I started studying.

124
00:07:13,083 --> 00:07:16,958
I didn't get on stage again
until I finished training.

125
00:07:18,667 --> 00:07:19,875
When I finished it,

126
00:07:21,417 --> 00:07:25,542
there was a very important man there
named José Luis Gómez,

127
00:07:26,208 --> 00:07:29,625
who is one of our great actors,
directors and producers,

128
00:07:30,667 --> 00:07:33,958
who called for auditions
for a play

129
00:07:34,042 --> 00:07:36,167
when I was already in the third year, finishing.

130
00:07:37,292 --> 00:07:39,042
The play was "Blood Weddings".

131
00:07:39,125 --> 00:07:42,667
Life rhymed,
Lorca appeared in my life again.

132
00:07:43,542 --> 00:07:45,875
I didn't want to take the tests

133
00:07:45,958 --> 00:07:48,208
because I remember
being happy at school,

134
00:07:48,292 --> 00:07:51,458
in that ideal placenta,

135
00:07:51,958 --> 00:07:54,792
where we talked about theater all day
and created.

136
00:07:54,875 --> 00:07:58,208
Going out and facing the profession

137
00:07:58,292 --> 00:08:01,917
for me was a world
that terrified me a lot

138
00:08:02,000 --> 00:08:04,625
because I didn't know how it worked.  I

139
00:08:04,708 --> 00:08:08,125
remember my teacher,
Pepe Estruch, told me:

140
00:08:08,208 --> 00:08:10,542
"Don't be afraid,
take this test

141
00:08:11,292 --> 00:08:12,625
and, if you fail,

142
00:08:14,250 --> 00:08:16,375
get out of here, because you have to get out,

143
00:08:16,458 --> 00:08:20,458
at some point you have to leave the
place where you are being educated

144
00:08:20,542 --> 00:08:22,708
and put into practice what you have learned."  I

145
00:08:23,333 --> 00:08:26,083
showed up for the tests
almost at gunpoint,

146
00:08:26,167 --> 00:08:27,417
because I didn't want to.

147
00:08:27,917 --> 00:08:29,792
Mr. Gomez caught me.

148
00:08:30,667 --> 00:08:32,958
Then,
this prevented me from doing the fourth year,

149
00:08:33,042 --> 00:08:34,792
which was already just a set-up.

150
00:08:35,292 --> 00:08:37,000
I gave up directing,

151
00:08:37,083 --> 00:08:39,958
but that opened the doors
to professional theater for me.

152
00:08:40,417 --> 00:08:43,000
Just finished, at 21 years old.  I

153
00:08:44,250 --> 00:08:46,250
realized that
what I had learned,

154
00:08:46,333 --> 00:08:48,667
I felt would be of no use to me.

155
00:08:48,750 --> 00:08:50,750
Because you believe, while you're learning,

156
00:08:50,833 --> 00:08:53,125
that what they teach you...
"What's that for?".

157
00:08:53,625 --> 00:08:55,833
Then it turned out
that I could apply everything I had learned

158
00:08:55,917 --> 00:08:58,333
to that job.

159
00:08:58,833 --> 00:09:02,000
Gómez himself told me
that I had good training,

160
00:09:02,083 --> 00:09:04,958
because I was aware
of my body in space,

161
00:09:05,042 --> 00:09:07,042
I knew how to manage my emotions,

162
00:09:07,875 --> 00:09:09,917
I put my voice in its place,

163
00:09:10,625 --> 00:09:13,500
I was able to understand
what a character meant

164
00:09:13,583 --> 00:09:15,417
within the structure of the performance.

165
00:09:15,500 --> 00:09:18,583
I began to realize
that all those subjects

166
00:09:18,667 --> 00:09:20,625
that I thought were not about theater,

167
00:09:20,708 --> 00:09:23,583
that were about studying, were super useful.

168
00:09:24,125 --> 00:09:27,417
So, well,
I joined that company

169
00:09:28,167 --> 00:09:30,083
and went on tour.

170
00:09:31,667 --> 00:09:34,792
Here was
another critical moment in my life

171
00:09:35,458 --> 00:09:39,375
because I decided that getting married
and moving out...

172
00:09:39,458 --> 00:09:40,958
made no sense.

173
00:09:41,583 --> 00:09:43,042
That the world was immense,

174
00:09:43,792 --> 00:09:46,167
that life was full of challenges,

175
00:09:47,000 --> 00:09:50,875
full of places to discover,
people to share with

176
00:09:52,500 --> 00:09:54,750
and what it meant to do my life.

177
00:09:55,583 --> 00:09:59,250
If I stayed home
with my wonderful boyfriend, it

178
00:09:59,958 --> 00:10:01,667
wouldn't work

179
00:10:01,750 --> 00:10:04,583
because it was like incompatible,
in a way.

180
00:10:04,667 --> 00:10:06,958
I wanted to keep running and walking.

181
00:10:07,042 --> 00:10:11,875
So, in a way, this marks
a turning point in my existence

182
00:10:12,542 --> 00:10:13,792
and, from there, I am

183
00:10:14,500 --> 00:10:17,458
lucky to have
never stopped working for

184
00:10:18,167 --> 00:10:19,917
more than six months in my life.

185
00:10:20,917 --> 00:10:25,625
Think about it, that was 20 or 21 years ago
and I'm 55.

186
00:10:26,042 --> 00:10:29,875
So, I just really appreciate

187
00:10:30,417 --> 00:10:33,917
the push from my teacher, who said,
"Take the tests."

188
00:10:34,458 --> 00:10:35,750
And to the guy who said:

189
00:10:35,833 --> 00:10:38,458
“There is the School
of Dramatic Art and Dance,”

190
00:10:38,542 --> 00:10:40,125
without knowing what he was doing.

191
00:10:41,417 --> 00:10:46,000
Or that's kind of the origin
of why I dedicate myself to this.  I've

192
00:10:46,500 --> 00:10:48,750
never stopped doing it

193
00:10:49,958 --> 00:10:51,458
because it's always different,

194
00:10:52,292 --> 00:10:54,083
because it has taught me a lot,

195
00:10:54,167 --> 00:10:57,958
I learn a lot every day
from the people I work with,

196
00:10:58,042 --> 00:11:01,750
from the people who sit in front
to watch a performance.  I have

197
00:11:02,792 --> 00:11:06,250
known countries, ways of thinking, it has

198
00:11:07,667 --> 00:11:09,750
opened my mind a lot, it has

199
00:11:09,833 --> 00:11:12,333
taught me a lot
and it continues to do so every day.  That's

200
00:11:12,417 --> 00:11:16,333
why I think I
never lose my desire for it

201
00:11:17,000 --> 00:11:20,292
and it continues to give me
enormous excitement and a huge sense of vertigo.

202
00:11:20,375 --> 00:11:22,542
Over the years, it scares me more and more.

203
00:11:23,500 --> 00:11:26,625
So anyone who thinks that this
is disappearing over the years is

204
00:11:26,708 --> 00:11:27,875
wrong.

205
00:11:27,958 --> 00:11:29,250
The fear increases

206
00:11:29,333 --> 00:11:33,333
because the more time you dedicate to it
and the more experience you have, the

207
00:11:33,417 --> 00:11:35,167
more responsibility you have.

208
00:11:35,250 --> 00:11:39,083
Before, you would make a character who would come out,
say "good afternoon" and leave.

209
00:11:39,167 --> 00:11:42,958
Now, you have a 50-page monologue.

210
00:11:43,500 --> 00:11:46,333
Therefore, the responsibility
is becoming greater and greater,

211
00:11:46,917 --> 00:11:49,042
and the fear is increasing.  You

212
00:11:49,125 --> 00:11:51,833
don't know what people expect from you,

213
00:11:51,917 --> 00:11:55,333
sometimes too much is expected, it
creates enormous insecurity,

214
00:11:55,417 --> 00:11:57,500
but, even so, it still makes me happy.  The

215
00:11:58,208 --> 00:12:02,208
day I lose my fear, I will stop doing it,

216
00:12:02,292 --> 00:12:05,125
because if it doesn't scare me, it
no longer interests me.

217
00:12:05,208 --> 00:12:06,583
I will feel like I already know everything

218
00:12:06,667 --> 00:12:09,042
and, if I know everything, I
don't deserve to work on this.

219
00:12:10,458 --> 00:12:13,250
So, well,
this is a bit of an introduction.

220
00:12:14,500 --> 00:12:15,833
From now on,

221
00:12:15,917 --> 00:12:19,500
if you want to ask me
anything, I

222
00:12:19,583 --> 00:12:21,417
will be happy to share.

223
00:12:21,500 --> 00:12:24,458
This is a chat, huh?
We talk to each other.

224
00:12:26,167 --> 00:12:27,625
Hello, Blanca, my name is Sandra.

225
00:12:27,708 --> 00:12:30,500
I am an actress
and theater teacher at Cuarta Pared.

226
00:12:31,167 --> 00:12:34,875
Well, at Cuarta
we also do extracurricular activities

227
00:12:34,958 --> 00:12:36,167
in schools.  We

228
00:12:36,250 --> 00:12:40,375
don't want the kids to
be Blanca Portillo or Robert de Niro,

229
00:12:41,042 --> 00:12:45,875
but, well, we do it because we believe it
's important for them

230
00:12:45,958 --> 00:12:48,500
and that it's very good for them to relate.

231
00:12:49,333 --> 00:12:52,000
My question is,
from your experience,

232
00:12:52,083 --> 00:12:54,333
what benefits do you think theater has

233
00:12:54,417 --> 00:12:57,000
on the children of our country?

234
00:12:58,125 --> 00:13:00,125
Ugh, a lot, I'm sure.

235
00:13:00,208 --> 00:13:03,500
In fact, many countries
have it as a compulsory subject.

236
00:13:04,417 --> 00:13:05,417
Mandatory.

237
00:13:06,042 --> 00:13:09,125
It's something everyone
should do once in their life.

238
00:13:09,208 --> 00:13:11,583
Everyone, no matter how old you are.

239
00:13:11,667 --> 00:13:14,250
But in childhood, with toddlers, it

240
00:13:14,750 --> 00:13:20,542
is a difficult time because they don't have the
tools to move through life.

241
00:13:20,625 --> 00:13:24,208
I have taught boys and girls.

242
00:13:24,917 --> 00:13:26,583
They lack tools.

243
00:13:26,667 --> 00:13:27,917
And there are many shames, it

244
00:13:28,000 --> 00:13:31,458
is a moment when they face the outside world

245
00:13:32,000 --> 00:13:35,708
when they have their own world at home,
more or less comfortable.

246
00:13:36,208 --> 00:13:37,875
Theater allows you, for starters, to

247
00:13:37,958 --> 00:13:40,792
connect with others
in a sincere way.

248
00:13:41,375 --> 00:13:45,667
This is a curious thing
that needs to be clarified.

249
00:13:46,208 --> 00:13:47,667
When you are at school,

250
00:13:48,833 --> 00:13:51,625
you share what
can be shared at school.

251
00:13:51,708 --> 00:13:53,000
But when you do theater,

252
00:13:53,083 --> 00:13:56,417
to begin with,
you have to share the fear, the emotion.

253
00:13:57,000 --> 00:13:58,750
You will work with your emotions,

254
00:13:59,417 --> 00:14:01,500
with your sense of the ridiculous.

255
00:14:02,375 --> 00:14:04,333
Losing the sense of the ridiculous.  We

256
00:14:04,958 --> 00:14:09,500
all try to be as sensible
and correct as possible in life, to

257
00:14:10,083 --> 00:14:12,125
do things more or less well,

258
00:14:12,833 --> 00:14:16,250
not to fall when we walk,
not to stumble, not to do...

259
00:14:16,958 --> 00:14:19,667
Nothing happens, the right to make mistakes,

260
00:14:19,750 --> 00:14:23,292
theatrical teachings
allow you to do this constantly.

261
00:14:23,375 --> 00:14:27,250
In fact, the basis of theater
is the mistake.

262
00:14:27,333 --> 00:14:31,458
You have to make mistakes to learn,
to be able to do it well.

263
00:14:31,542 --> 00:14:35,875
Error, hit, error.
Research how to do it better.

264
00:14:35,958 --> 00:14:39,083
Therefore,
their minds are opened, they lose their fear.  I

265
00:14:39,167 --> 00:14:42,500
remember that, while teaching, there
was a boy who was,

266
00:14:42,583 --> 00:14:45,125
let's say, the bad guy in the group.

267
00:14:45,208 --> 00:14:47,000
There are always roles that go...

268
00:14:47,083 --> 00:14:51,042
There was a dwarf
who was like the most cocky of them all.

269
00:14:52,208 --> 00:14:54,500
The rest were a little afraid of him.

270
00:14:54,583 --> 00:14:57,292
When he made a joke, everyone laughed.

271
00:14:57,375 --> 00:15:00,042
I decided to give him
the most serious character,

272
00:15:00,125 --> 00:15:03,542
the most sensitive,
the one who was the saddest.  He

273
00:15:03,625 --> 00:15:05,625
discovered, within himself,

274
00:15:05,708 --> 00:15:08,708
that not only did this
not make him lose authority

275
00:15:08,792 --> 00:15:10,083
over his peers,

276
00:15:10,167 --> 00:15:13,000
but it showed the rest a side he did

277
00:15:14,500 --> 00:15:16,708
n't know he had

278
00:15:16,792 --> 00:15:19,667
and that made the rest truly
love him

279
00:15:19,750 --> 00:15:21,375
or truly admire him.

280
00:15:21,458 --> 00:15:23,375
He took it very seriously

281
00:15:23,458 --> 00:15:25,917
and began working on it
with great dedication.

282
00:15:26,458 --> 00:15:29,417
With that, he began to
be the leader in a different way,

283
00:15:29,500 --> 00:15:32,875
in a much more honest way,
because he cried,

284
00:15:32,958 --> 00:15:35,458
because he was able to cry
in front of his friends.

285
00:15:36,000 --> 00:15:40,000
And that was like a carom,
that's what happened to the rest.

286
00:15:40,500 --> 00:15:42,333
Well, on that occasion,

287
00:15:43,625 --> 00:15:45,750
I had a problem
with the teachers

288
00:15:45,833 --> 00:15:49,042
because the children wanted to
stop doing all kinds of classes,

289
00:15:49,125 --> 00:15:50,458
all kinds of activities,

290
00:15:50,542 --> 00:15:53,000
because they only wanted to
do theater classes,

291
00:15:53,083 --> 00:15:56,083
and the teachers told me:
“It's becoming a problem

292
00:15:56,167 --> 00:15:58,542
because the parents want them to
study other things.”

293
00:15:58,625 --> 00:16:01,417
In short, it opens up many paths for them,
especially in the mind.

294
00:16:02,083 --> 00:16:04,458
And in their way
of relating to others

295
00:16:04,542 --> 00:16:06,000
and losing their modesty.

296
00:16:07,750 --> 00:16:10,833
Sometimes they say
that actors are the biggest liars.

297
00:16:10,917 --> 00:16:12,750
It is said that an actor lies.  I

298
00:16:12,833 --> 00:16:16,583
think it's the opposite,
we are the people who lie the least.  I

299
00:16:17,375 --> 00:16:21,000
think that citizens in general,
people in general,

300
00:16:21,083 --> 00:16:22,333
build characters for ourselves

301
00:16:22,417 --> 00:16:24,875
that are often not true at all.  We pretend to be

302
00:16:24,958 --> 00:16:27,125
strong when we are fragile, we pretend to be

303
00:16:27,208 --> 00:16:30,208
fragile
when in reality everything is the same for us, we

304
00:16:30,292 --> 00:16:32,583
build a character for ourselves outwardly

305
00:16:33,250 --> 00:16:36,083
and try to be consistent
with this character

306
00:16:36,167 --> 00:16:37,458
throughout our lives.

307
00:16:37,917 --> 00:16:41,500
However, actors live,
precisely, without the mask on,

308
00:16:42,167 --> 00:16:46,000
bringing out from us everything that we
sometimes don't want to see that we have.

309
00:16:46,083 --> 00:16:50,542
This offers children a chance
to see themselves in a different way.

310
00:16:51,583 --> 00:16:53,625
Losing the sense of the ridiculous.

311
00:16:53,708 --> 00:16:56,500
We do a lot of things
or stop doing them

312
00:16:56,583 --> 00:16:58,917
because we are ashamed,
because we are embarrassed.

313
00:16:59,000 --> 00:17:01,292
"I won't be able to do this."  Why not?

314
00:17:01,375 --> 00:17:05,583
There's always a: "Why not?",
and I think that's very healthy.

315
00:17:05,667 --> 00:17:07,958
Then,
on the other hand, when you do theater... I

316
00:17:09,250 --> 00:17:12,167
explained it to them,
and they were very young, right?

317
00:17:12,917 --> 00:17:15,792
We did
Shakespeare's "A Midsummer Night's Dream."

318
00:17:16,708 --> 00:17:20,250
Inevitably, you
start talking about mythology,

319
00:17:21,250 --> 00:17:25,000
talking about Shakespeare
as an author and not just a playwright, you

320
00:17:25,708 --> 00:17:27,375
start talking about his time.

321
00:17:27,958 --> 00:17:32,542
Therefore, they begin to learn
a lot of collateral things

322
00:17:32,625 --> 00:17:35,042
that are related
to general education,

323
00:17:35,125 --> 00:17:38,917
but they see them through them,
through their own bodies.

324
00:17:39,000 --> 00:17:42,875
What Puck represents in the play,
which is a kind of goblin,

325
00:17:43,458 --> 00:17:46,083
has its value
and meaning within the story

326
00:17:46,167 --> 00:17:47,458
and they begin to understand it.

327
00:17:47,542 --> 00:17:50,542
"Where can I learn this?
What books are there about this?"  Their

328
00:17:50,625 --> 00:17:54,875
curiosity is awakened
in an incredible way.

329
00:17:54,958 --> 00:17:58,375
Then they begin to learn that,
without the other, you are nothing,

330
00:17:59,000 --> 00:18:00,500
and that is also important.  It's

331
00:18:00,583 --> 00:18:02,500
not about being the best, it's

332
00:18:02,583 --> 00:18:06,000
about being a strong link
in a strong chain.

333
00:18:06,625 --> 00:18:08,375
A team is formed,

334
00:18:08,458 --> 00:18:11,125
a group is formed
in which everyone helps each other

335
00:18:11,208 --> 00:18:13,292
and rivalries are eliminated.  There

336
00:18:13,375 --> 00:18:16,333
is always someone who says:
“Why do I have fewer sentences?

337
00:18:16,417 --> 00:18:18,042
I want to have more sentences.”  We

338
00:18:18,125 --> 00:18:20,375
all have a protagonist inside.

339
00:18:20,875 --> 00:18:23,875
But, well, when they realize it...
You give them responsibilities

340
00:18:23,958 --> 00:18:29,208
and they realize that they don't have to be
the protagonist in the role.

341
00:18:29,292 --> 00:18:32,125
Because then you have a lot more work
to do behind the scenes too.

342
00:18:32,208 --> 00:18:34,375
You're the one who will help him when he comes out,

343
00:18:34,458 --> 00:18:37,417
you're in charge of the costumes,
you help him...

344
00:18:37,500 --> 00:18:40,333
The feeling of working in collaboration,
all together,

345
00:18:40,417 --> 00:18:42,042
which is the basis of theater,

346
00:18:42,583 --> 00:18:44,375
teaches them a lot.

347
00:18:44,458 --> 00:18:47,917
I'm telling you, I know they
ended up telling me:

348
00:18:48,000 --> 00:18:50,500
"Don't come anymore
because they don't want to do anything else."  And they did it

349
00:18:51,542 --> 00:18:52,583
all.

350
00:18:52,667 --> 00:18:55,333
They made the costumes,
the music, they did everything.  It

351
00:18:56,000 --> 00:18:59,458
was beautiful to see how girls
who didn't dare to say a word

352
00:19:00,792 --> 00:19:04,708
ended up on stage
playing wonderful characters.

353
00:19:04,792 --> 00:19:06,292
This is very nice to see.

354
00:19:07,833 --> 00:19:10,125
There is one aspect
that I think is very important,

355
00:19:10,208 --> 00:19:12,625
which is
learning to speak in public

356
00:19:13,208 --> 00:19:15,542
and know how to convey ideas.  I

357
00:19:16,875 --> 00:19:21,042
don't know if you've ever had
this fear of public speaking.

358
00:19:22,458 --> 00:19:25,000
What would you say to a child or young person

359
00:19:25,917 --> 00:19:27,958
who has this fear?

360
00:19:28,042 --> 00:19:30,667
Speaking in public
is a very special thing.  You

361
00:19:31,750 --> 00:19:35,833
must keep in mind that,
99% of the time,

362
00:19:35,917 --> 00:19:38,333
an actor does not speak
with his own voice,

363
00:19:39,375 --> 00:19:41,125
but through a character.

364
00:19:41,708 --> 00:19:43,667
So, I know what to say, I've

365
00:19:44,667 --> 00:19:46,333
already learned it.  And

366
00:19:46,417 --> 00:19:50,000
I don't say it, she or he says it.

367
00:19:51,917 --> 00:19:54,250
This takes away half of your problem.

368
00:19:55,500 --> 00:19:58,000
For me, public speaking
is what we are doing now.

369
00:19:58,083 --> 00:20:01,708
I'm facing a series of people
who are looking at me

370
00:20:02,458 --> 00:20:07,000
and I don't have a script written, I
don't know what I'm going to say

371
00:20:07,083 --> 00:20:08,500
and I'm the one talking.

372
00:20:08,583 --> 00:20:10,750
This time it's me, not a character.

373
00:20:11,458 --> 00:20:15,583
This has
caused me enormous...

374
00:20:16,500 --> 00:20:18,958
excitement and terrible fear today.

375
00:20:19,042 --> 00:20:21,000
I'm very nervous, I told you.

376
00:20:21,083 --> 00:20:23,708
It is the first thing you have to assume

377
00:20:23,792 --> 00:20:25,708
when you have to speak in public.  It

378
00:20:25,792 --> 00:20:28,250
makes you nervous, who doesn't get nervous?

379
00:20:28,333 --> 00:20:30,458
Because nobody wants to look ridiculous,

380
00:20:30,542 --> 00:20:32,500
that's normal, right?

381
00:20:32,583 --> 00:20:35,833
Nothing really happens,
ridiculousness is a relative thing.

382
00:20:35,917 --> 00:20:37,500
I try...

383
00:20:37,583 --> 00:20:39,958
It's true that we speak
with a text that doesn't belong to us,

384
00:20:40,042 --> 00:20:45,417
but, whether you like it or not,
there are 400 people sitting

385
00:20:45,500 --> 00:20:46,500
like this,

386
00:20:47,208 --> 00:20:48,792
waiting to see what you say.

387
00:20:50,292 --> 00:20:52,917
Anyone who doesn't get nervous about this
is crazy.

388
00:20:54,000 --> 00:20:57,125
You have to be very crazy
for this not to make you nervous.

389
00:20:57,208 --> 00:20:59,792
I think it's a problem, not with the kids,

390
00:20:59,875 --> 00:21:02,042
I think it's also a teacher...

391
00:21:02,875 --> 00:21:05,417
You arrive at class on the first day,
I imagine,

392
00:21:06,042 --> 00:21:08,792
and you see a number of people there, like that.

393
00:21:09,667 --> 00:21:11,167
And you say: “Hello, how are we doing?”  It's

394
00:21:11,875 --> 00:21:14,292
one thing to be in the habit of doing it

395
00:21:14,375 --> 00:21:16,458
and another thing to not be afraid of it.  It's

396
00:21:16,542 --> 00:21:18,167
always scary,

397
00:21:18,250 --> 00:21:21,208
and that's something
I think we need to accept.

398
00:21:21,583 --> 00:21:24,875
When someone has to speak,
if you ever have to:

399
00:21:25,375 --> 00:21:27,917
“Hello, I’m scared.”  Nothing happens.

400
00:21:28,583 --> 00:21:29,708
On the other hand, it's

401
00:21:30,833 --> 00:21:34,042
good to know
that nothing happens if you make a mistake,

402
00:21:34,125 --> 00:21:36,000
nothing happens if you come up empty.

403
00:21:36,083 --> 00:21:38,667
Nobody will die,
nobody will sit there and go “boom!”.

404
00:21:39,333 --> 00:21:42,958
Do you know?  There is no danger, there
is no real risk.

405
00:21:43,500 --> 00:21:47,667
The only risk is your own fear
of looking foolish or ridiculous,

406
00:21:48,208 --> 00:21:51,417
the level you set for yourself,
the bar.

407
00:21:52,792 --> 00:21:55,208
There is something that is sometimes
difficult for us to think about

408
00:21:55,292 --> 00:21:56,583
when we speak in public:

409
00:21:56,667 --> 00:21:59,958
the people who are there
are willing to listen.

410
00:22:00,875 --> 00:22:03,167
In a theater, because they paid.

411
00:22:03,250 --> 00:22:05,500
People don't always pay to listen to you.

412
00:22:05,583 --> 00:22:08,000
Sometimes I think about it
and it makes me very nervous.  They

413
00:22:08,083 --> 00:22:09,792
paid to listen.

414
00:22:09,875 --> 00:22:12,292
Therefore, they also have a provision there.  They

415
00:22:13,000 --> 00:22:15,333
are not a mass of people, they

416
00:22:15,833 --> 00:22:17,250
are individuals,

417
00:22:17,333 --> 00:22:20,667
they are human beings
with a name and surname, each of them.

418
00:22:21,250 --> 00:22:23,292
It's another thing we
often forget.

419
00:22:23,375 --> 00:22:26,042
Public speaking
is speaking to a mass of people.

420
00:22:27,417 --> 00:22:31,333
They are little people with feelings,
with their nerves too.

421
00:22:31,417 --> 00:22:34,417
I imagine that today you
also have something like:

422
00:22:34,500 --> 00:22:38,417
“Well, let's see, I'm here, let's
see what this woman has to tell us.”

423
00:22:38,500 --> 00:22:43,208
You too find yourself in an
uncomfortable situation in your living room.

424
00:22:43,792 --> 00:22:45,208
Therefore, when you think

425
00:22:45,292 --> 00:22:48,083
that the other person is in
almost the same situation as you, you

426
00:22:48,167 --> 00:22:51,333
begin to lose your fear, to relax.  It

427
00:22:51,875 --> 00:22:54,542
is clear that you must know
what you want to explain.

428
00:22:55,833 --> 00:22:57,708
I don't know right now,

429
00:22:57,792 --> 00:23:00,292
because I'm seeing what you're asking me

430
00:23:00,375 --> 00:23:02,625
and I'm building a speech
as I go.

431
00:23:03,167 --> 00:23:05,167
But, well, that's also what life gives you,

432
00:23:05,250 --> 00:23:06,792
the years, the experience

433
00:23:06,875 --> 00:23:09,917
and having a real desire to
share something.

434
00:23:10,000 --> 00:23:12,208
This is another thing
that really takes away your fear,

435
00:23:12,958 --> 00:23:16,042
the idea of: “I want to share
what I have with you.”

436
00:23:16,792 --> 00:23:18,583
You are here to listen

437
00:23:18,667 --> 00:23:20,750
and I am here
to give you everything I have,

438
00:23:21,417 --> 00:23:24,083
and it brings me well-being and pleasure to do so.

439
00:23:24,917 --> 00:23:26,708
Our work, that of actors, does not exist

440
00:23:26,792 --> 00:23:28,833
without you,
the viewer.

441
00:23:29,417 --> 00:23:33,083
A teacher's job,
without students, is meaningless.

442
00:23:33,750 --> 00:23:37,458
Anyone who gives a speech
has an audience, they

443
00:23:37,542 --> 00:23:39,250
have people who are listening to them,

444
00:23:39,333 --> 00:23:43,000
an audience that is there,
waiting for what they will say.  You

445
00:23:43,500 --> 00:23:45,583
will be nervous, you will be scared,

446
00:23:45,667 --> 00:23:49,542
but you are a human being who wants to share
things with other human beings.  There

447
00:23:50,583 --> 00:23:52,333
are teachers here, right?

448
00:23:52,833 --> 00:23:54,542
Are you a teacher?
-I do.

449
00:23:55,250 --> 00:23:57,125
Can you come for a moment, please?

450
00:24:00,125 --> 00:24:03,083
You're used to being in front of people.

451
00:24:03,167 --> 00:24:05,250
-Yes.
-Oh, yes?  And usually...

452
00:24:05,333 --> 00:24:11,125
Let's see, a teacher, sometimes,
those who listen to him are forced to.  It's

453
00:24:12,125 --> 00:24:13,917
not like they're paying to be there.

454
00:24:15,208 --> 00:24:17,792
But, in general, they
are there because they have to be there

455
00:24:17,875 --> 00:24:20,375
and they know they have to and they want to.

456
00:24:20,458 --> 00:24:24,833
There is a difference,
I imagine, tell me if I'm wrong.  It

457
00:24:26,083 --> 00:24:27,750
's very different to see a mass

458
00:24:29,167 --> 00:24:30,750
and glance over it

459
00:24:30,833 --> 00:24:33,208
than to look at them one by one, right?
-Yes, totally.  Try

460
00:24:33,292 --> 00:24:35,625
it, one by one,

461
00:24:36,333 --> 00:24:38,958
and pay attention to a small detail
of each one.

462
00:24:40,417 --> 00:24:42,458
Everyone has their eyes on you.  They

463
00:24:43,750 --> 00:24:45,417
don't look the other way, do they?
-No.

464
00:24:47,208 --> 00:24:48,708
-That's interesting.
-Very much.

465
00:24:48,792 --> 00:24:50,625
-They are waiting for you.
-Well, from you.

466
00:24:50,708 --> 00:24:53,042
-No, now they're looking at you.
-Yes, too.

467
00:24:53,125 --> 00:24:54,583
Now they're looking at you.  They

468
00:24:55,250 --> 00:24:56,292
look at you.

469
00:24:57,458 --> 00:25:00,292
He, the other and she.

470
00:25:00,375 --> 00:25:02,917
You see her moving a foot,
she's a little nervous.

471
00:25:04,375 --> 00:25:05,708
You look at them

472
00:25:06,417 --> 00:25:08,583
and a connection occurs.
-Yes.

473
00:25:09,083 --> 00:25:10,667
When you teach, do you

474
00:25:10,750 --> 00:25:13,542
look at the whole class
or at them individually?

475
00:25:13,625 --> 00:25:15,958
-No, it is looked at individually.
-Oh, yes?

476
00:25:16,042 --> 00:25:18,417
And that makes you lose a little bit of fear.

477
00:25:18,500 --> 00:25:20,833
-And that they are with you more.
-Oh, friend.

478
00:25:21,625 --> 00:25:24,083
This is one of the great challenges
of public speaking:

479
00:25:24,167 --> 00:25:25,458
getting attention.

480
00:25:26,583 --> 00:25:27,792
Capture it.

481
00:25:27,875 --> 00:25:30,292
The only way
to get attention is to give.

482
00:25:31,083 --> 00:25:31,958
Give.

483
00:25:32,542 --> 00:25:34,958
It is an act of generosity.

484
00:25:35,458 --> 00:25:38,375
And this is very noticeable in politicians.  Have
n't you noticed,

485
00:25:38,917 --> 00:25:40,958
when a politician doesn't speak for us?  He

486
00:25:41,833 --> 00:25:45,000
does this, looks inward
and speaks for himself

487
00:25:45,917 --> 00:25:47,125
or for a mass.

488
00:25:47,625 --> 00:25:50,500
When someone looks at you, you

489
00:25:51,250 --> 00:25:54,750
say: “Oh, it’s for me,

?  You

"But do you really

I have to shoot at seven, I

I think that, despite all the things I've

That's why I always say

We lack a lot of communication, it
's a shame.  I'm

n't listen, we

I bless

Free of charge, for nothing, because yes.

You see someone looking bad

1544

I have the privilege of communicating

Much more than putting on a show

1548
01:21:52,417 --> 01:21:53,708
Much more important.

1549
01:21:57,833 --> 01:22:01,875
Well, anyway, looking into your eyes, I

1550

thank you

1
00:00:21,708 --> 00:00:24,083
¿Qué tal? Encantada de veros por aquí.

2
00:00:24,167 --> 00:00:26,958
Es un placer estar con vosotros.

3
00:00:28,083 --> 00:00:31,292
Estoy un poco nerviosa,
lo digo ya para que lo sepáis.

4
00:00:31,375 --> 00:00:35,458
Y me encantaría que pasemos un buen rato
juntos conversando.

5
00:00:35,542 --> 00:00:38,625
No sé si lo que tengo que contaros
os puede ser de interés,

6
00:00:38,708 --> 00:00:40,000
pero lo voy a intentar.

7
00:00:41,042 --> 00:00:43,083
Mi nombre es Blanca Portillo,

8
00:00:43,167 --> 00:00:45,375
también conocida
como Rojiblanca Portillo.

9
00:00:46,500 --> 00:00:49,875
Soy del Atlético de Madrid
de toda la vida.

10
00:00:50,375 --> 00:00:53,292
Y me declaro adicta a la interpretación.

11
00:00:53,750 --> 00:00:56,250
Es lo que más me gusta en el mundo

12
00:00:56,917 --> 00:01:01,667
y a lo que dedico todo mi tiempo,
toda mi energía y toda mi pasión.

13
00:01:03,042 --> 00:01:06,208
Me encantaría compartir con vosotros
cómo empecé en esto

14
00:01:06,292 --> 00:01:08,083
y por qué lo amo como lo amo.

15
00:01:09,042 --> 00:01:10,875
Primero, porque me cambió la vida.

16
00:01:10,958 --> 00:01:13,750
Y segundo,
porque es lo que más me ha enseñado

17
00:01:14,333 --> 00:01:16,917
en todas las vivencias que he tenido.

18
00:01:17,000 --> 00:01:20,333
Ha sido mi guía, lo que me ha abierto
las puertas al mundo,

19
00:01:20,417 --> 00:01:23,042
lo que ha hecho
que me conozca a mí misma mejor,

20
00:01:23,125 --> 00:01:24,542
y a los demás.

21
00:01:24,625 --> 00:01:27,125
Yo soy la cuarta hija de ocho.

22
00:01:27,667 --> 00:01:31,375
Somos ocho hermanos
de una familia de lo más normal.

23
00:01:32,250 --> 00:01:36,125
Más bien tirando a una economía baja.

24
00:01:37,167 --> 00:01:39,917
Mi padre falleció
cuando yo tenía 18 años.

25
00:01:41,958 --> 00:01:45,208
Empecé a estudiar formación profesional
al terminar la EGB.

26
00:01:45,292 --> 00:01:46,792
Lo que entonces era la EGB.

27
00:01:47,583 --> 00:01:50,583
Y estudié formación profesional
de Administrativo.

28
00:01:51,167 --> 00:01:53,542
Cuando tenía 13 o 14 años

29
00:01:53,625 --> 00:01:56,083
no sabía muy bien
lo que quería ser en la vida,

30
00:01:56,167 --> 00:01:58,125
no tenía ni la más remota idea.

31
00:01:58,208 --> 00:02:01,458
Me encantaba la idea
de contar historias,

32
00:02:02,042 --> 00:02:05,833
porque reconozco que he sido lectora
desde muy chiquitita.

33
00:02:07,375 --> 00:02:08,458
Porque, probablemente,

34
00:02:08,542 --> 00:02:10,542
como no me gustaba mucho
la vida que tenía,

35
00:02:11,625 --> 00:02:14,458
la mejor manera de escapar era leyendo.

36
00:02:15,750 --> 00:02:18,625
Yo me metía dentro de un libro
y vivía ese libro,

37
00:02:18,708 --> 00:02:20,417
y vivía lo que vivían los personajes

38
00:02:20,500 --> 00:02:23,708
y me trasladaba a otros lugares,
a otros mundos,

39
00:02:23,792 --> 00:02:26,375
a otras ciudades, a otros paraísos,

40
00:02:26,458 --> 00:02:30,167
y eso me hacía escaparme de una realidad
que, ya os digo, no me gustaba mucho.

41
00:02:31,750 --> 00:02:33,417
Después de estudiar
formación profesional

42
00:02:33,500 --> 00:02:37,042
decidí que si quería contar historias

43
00:02:37,125 --> 00:02:40,292
o estar en contacto con la gente,
que eso me gustaba mucho también,

44
00:02:41,708 --> 00:02:44,625
la mejor profesión que podía elegir,
no os riais,

45
00:02:45,417 --> 00:02:48,375
era azafata de congresos.
¿Por qué? Pues no lo sé.

46
00:02:48,958 --> 00:02:53,042
Me parecía interesante estar con gente,
poder compartir,

47
00:02:53,125 --> 00:02:56,000
y si tenías un congreso,
pues seguramente aprendería cosas

48
00:02:56,083 --> 00:02:59,583
y podría, bueno, pues crecer,
de alguna manera.

49
00:03:00,000 --> 00:03:02,292
Empecé a estudiar esto.

50
00:03:04,042 --> 00:03:06,208
Hice unos cuantos congresos

51
00:03:06,292 --> 00:03:08,292
en los que me aburrí como una ostra.

52
00:03:09,167 --> 00:03:11,208
Te ponían un uniforme
y lo único que tenías que hacer

53
00:03:11,292 --> 00:03:14,625
era decir buenas tardes, pase por aquí,
buenas tardes, pase por aquí...

54
00:03:14,708 --> 00:03:17,833
Y aquello no era ni contar historias
ni estar con la gente.

55
00:03:17,917 --> 00:03:20,167
Pero tuve la fortuna
de tener un profesor.

56
00:03:20,792 --> 00:03:23,500
Un profesor que nos daba
Geografía turística.

57
00:03:24,292 --> 00:03:28,042
Y él tenía un grupo de teatro.

58
00:03:28,750 --> 00:03:31,417
Yo no tenía ninguna relación
con el teatro.

59
00:03:31,500 --> 00:03:34,375
En mi vida personal...
Sé que mi madre y mi abuela

60
00:03:34,458 --> 00:03:37,375
eran gente a la que le gustaba
ir al teatro y al cine,

61
00:03:38,417 --> 00:03:41,083
pero yo no había ido
más que una vez en mi vida.

62
00:03:41,958 --> 00:03:43,208
No más.

63
00:03:43,292 --> 00:03:45,333
Entonces,
yo me enamoré de ese profesor.

64
00:03:45,417 --> 00:03:48,208
Era tan fascinante todo lo que contaba,

65
00:03:48,292 --> 00:03:50,125
era tan inteligente, tan maravilloso...

66
00:03:50,208 --> 00:03:51,958
Fue un amor muy platónico, no os creáis.

67
00:03:52,833 --> 00:03:57,375
Sentarte a escucharle
era como leer un libro,

68
00:03:57,458 --> 00:03:58,625
viajar a otros lugares.

69
00:03:58,708 --> 00:04:01,875
Te abría la cabeza, te hacía analizar
las cosas de una manera diferente.

70
00:04:02,250 --> 00:04:06,208
Entonces, él iba eligiendo a personas

71
00:04:06,917 --> 00:04:09,292
para que entraran en su grupo de teatro,

72
00:04:09,375 --> 00:04:12,833
que eran un poco los selectos,
el grupo de los exquisitos.

73
00:04:13,500 --> 00:04:15,125
Durante el primer año yo no entré,

74
00:04:15,208 --> 00:04:20,083
y al segundo año me invitó a participar
en el grupo de teatro.

75
00:04:21,167 --> 00:04:24,667
Yo por aquel entonces estaba
muy obsesionada con Lorca.

76
00:04:25,792 --> 00:04:27,667
Siempre me ha gustado,
desde que era muy jovencita,

77
00:04:27,750 --> 00:04:30,833
y toda su historia alrededor,
todo lo que le ocurrió.

78
00:04:31,417 --> 00:04:35,333
Y ese momento de la historia de España,
que me tenía como muy fascinada.

79
00:04:35,417 --> 00:04:39,208
Un poeta tan maravilloso que de repente
lo perdimos de una manera tan extraña.

80
00:04:40,417 --> 00:04:43,708
Y él estaba haciendo una obra
sobre Lorca, curiosamente.

81
00:04:44,458 --> 00:04:46,917
Entonces yo,
con tal de estar en ese grupo, dije:

82
00:04:47,000 --> 00:04:48,250
"Pues vámonos para allá".

83
00:04:49,417 --> 00:04:53,417
Yo tenía un novio
con el que me iba a casar.

84
00:04:54,417 --> 00:04:55,917
Teníamos un piso ya,

85
00:04:56,000 --> 00:04:58,208
teníamos un montón de cosas
más o menos hechas.

86
00:04:58,292 --> 00:05:02,167
Yo tenía 18 años, era muy joven,
pero lo tenía como muy claro,

87
00:05:02,250 --> 00:05:04,625
que era, de alguna manera,
el hombre de mi vida,

88
00:05:05,292 --> 00:05:08,542
y que, por otro lado,
estaba mi profesión o mi carrera.

89
00:05:08,625 --> 00:05:10,875
Entonces,
cuando empezamos a hacer teatro,

90
00:05:11,750 --> 00:05:14,042
yo descubrí un mundo

91
00:05:14,667 --> 00:05:16,875
completamente extraño

92
00:05:18,083 --> 00:05:21,375
que me hacía viajar de verdad,
no leyendo,

93
00:05:21,958 --> 00:05:25,833
el personaje era yo
y la que vivía las cosas era yo.

94
00:05:26,708 --> 00:05:30,083
Hubo un día en un ensayo que alguien
que estaba viendo ese ensayo

95
00:05:30,167 --> 00:05:34,042

"Me has emocionado mucho".

96
00:05:35,458 --> 00:05:38,500
Y aquello ya se convirtió
en el colmo de los colmos,

97
00:05:38,583 --> 00:05:43,250
pensar que la emoción que yo sentía
mientras hacía ese trabajo,

98
00:05:43,750 --> 00:05:46,458
o esa investigación,
porque ni siquiera era un trabajo,

99
00:05:47,250 --> 00:05:49,667
traspasaba mi propio ser

100
00:05:49,750 --> 00:05:53,875
y conectaba con otro que estaba enfrente
y le producía una emoción,

101
00:05:54,542 --> 00:05:58,375

"No puede ser, esto es magia.

102
00:05:58,792 --> 00:06:02,625
O sea, lo que yo siento,
puede sentirlo alguien fuera,

103
00:06:02,708 --> 00:06:06,125
diciendo cosas y viviendo cosas,
no leyéndolas".

104
00:06:06,958 --> 00:06:10,958
A partir de ese momento decidí
que eso era lo que quería hacer.

105
00:06:12,125 --> 00:06:15,375
Ahí se aunaban las dos cosas
que más me interesaban,

106
00:06:15,458 --> 00:06:17,708
que era contar historias

107
00:06:19,083 --> 00:06:20,625
y estar con gente,

108
00:06:20,708 --> 00:06:25,125
porque gran parte de este trabajo
tiene que ver con la idea de equipo.

109
00:06:26,292 --> 00:06:28,708
La interpretación no existe
como algo en sí mismo,

110
00:06:28,792 --> 00:06:29,833
tú contigo mismo,

111
00:06:29,917 --> 00:06:32,000
sino que tiene que haber primero
un receptor,

112
00:06:32,083 --> 00:06:34,250
y después,
gente con la que compartes eso.

113
00:06:35,583 --> 00:06:39,167
Recuerdo que yo no sabía
que esto se estudiaba.

114
00:06:40,292 --> 00:06:44,208
Entonces, ese novio que tenía me dijo:
"Pues sí, hay un lugar que se llama

115
00:06:44,292 --> 00:06:47,542
la Real Escuela Superior
de Arte Dramático y Danza de Madrid".

116
00:06:48,375 --> 00:06:50,167
"¿Y allí qué se estudia?".

117
00:06:50,625 --> 00:06:52,750
"Pues vamos a verlo".
Yo me acerqué.

118
00:06:52,833 --> 00:06:56,333
Entonces estaba en la plaza de Ópera,
donde hoy está el Teatro Real.

119
00:06:57,125 --> 00:06:58,417
Me presenté a unas pruebas

120
00:06:58,500 --> 00:07:02,125
donde te pedían
que interpretaras un texto en verso

121
00:07:02,917 --> 00:07:05,792
e hicieras una improvisación
y un examen escrito.

122
00:07:06,500 --> 00:07:10,042
Y me cogieron, y aprobé.

123
00:07:10,750 --> 00:07:12,667
Y entonces empecé a estudiar.

124
00:07:13,083 --> 00:07:16,958
No volví a subirme a un escenario
hasta que no acabé la formación.

125
00:07:18,667 --> 00:07:19,875
Y al terminar,

126
00:07:21,417 --> 00:07:25,542
había un señor por ahí muy importante
que se llamaba José Luis Gómez,

127
00:07:26,208 --> 00:07:29,625
que es uno de nuestros grandes actores
y directores, y productores,

128
00:07:30,667 --> 00:07:33,958
que convocó pruebas
para una obra de teatro

129
00:07:34,042 --> 00:07:36,167
cuando yo ya estaba en tercero,
terminando.

130
00:07:37,292 --> 00:07:39,042
La obra era "Bodas de sangre".

131
00:07:39,125 --> 00:07:42,667
La vida rimaba,
volvía a aparecer Lorca en mi vida.

132
00:07:43,542 --> 00:07:45,875
Y yo no quería presentarme a las pruebas

133
00:07:45,958 --> 00:07:48,208
porque estaba metida
en la escuela tan feliz,

134
00:07:48,292 --> 00:07:51,458
metida en aquella placenta ideal,

135
00:07:51,958 --> 00:07:54,792
donde estábamos todo el día
hablando de teatro, y creando,

136
00:07:54,875 --> 00:07:58,208
y salir ahí afuera
era enfrentarse a la profesión,

137
00:07:58,292 --> 00:08:01,917
que para mí era como un mundo
que me producía mucho terror

138
00:08:02,000 --> 00:08:04,625
porque no sabía cómo funcionaba eso.

139
00:08:04,708 --> 00:08:08,125
Y yo me acuerdo que mi maestro,
Pepe Estruch, me dijo:

140
00:08:08,208 --> 00:08:10,542
"No tengas miedo,
preséntate a esa prueba

141
00:08:11,292 --> 00:08:12,625
y si te coge,

142
00:08:14,250 --> 00:08:16,375
sal de aquí,
porque tienes que salir,

143
00:08:16,458 --> 00:08:20,458
en algún momento tienes que salir
del lugar donde te están educando

144
00:08:20,542 --> 00:08:22,708
y poner en práctica
lo que has aprendido".

145
00:08:23,333 --> 00:08:26,083
Me presenté a las pruebas
casi a punta de pistola,

146
00:08:26,167 --> 00:08:27,417
porque yo no quería.

147
00:08:27,917 --> 00:08:29,792
Y el señor Gómez me cogió.

148
00:08:30,667 --> 00:08:32,958
Entonces, eso me impidió
hacer el cuarto curso,

149
00:08:33,042 --> 00:08:34,792
que era ya solamente un montaje.

150
00:08:35,292 --> 00:08:37,000
Tuve que renunciar al montaje,

151
00:08:37,083 --> 00:08:39,958
pero me abrió las puertas
al teatro profesional.

152
00:08:40,417 --> 00:08:43,000
Nada más terminar, con 21 años.

153
00:08:44,250 --> 00:08:46,250
Me di cuenta
de que lo que había aprendido,

154
00:08:46,333 --> 00:08:48,667
yo sentía
que no me iba a valer para nada.

155
00:08:48,750 --> 00:08:50,750
Porque uno cree,
mientras está aprendiendo,

156
00:08:50,833 --> 00:08:53,125
que lo que te enseñan...
"¿Y esto para qué?".

157
00:08:53,625 --> 00:08:55,833
Y luego resultó
que todo lo que había aprendido

158
00:08:55,917 --> 00:08:58,333
lo podía volcar en ese trabajo.

159
00:08:58,833 --> 00:09:02,000
Y el propio Gómez me dijo
que tenía una buena formación,

160
00:09:02,083 --> 00:09:04,958
porque era consciente de mi cuerpo
en el espacio,

161
00:09:05,042 --> 00:09:07,042
sabía manejar mis emociones,

162
00:09:07,875 --> 00:09:09,917
la voz estaba colocada en su sitio,

163
00:09:10,625 --> 00:09:13,500
era capaz de entender
lo que significaba un personaje

164
00:09:13,583 --> 00:09:15,417
dentro de la estructura de la función.

165
00:09:15,500 --> 00:09:18,583
Empecé a darme cuenta
de que todas aquellas asignaturas

166
00:09:18,667 --> 00:09:20,625
que a mí me parecía
que no eran de teatro,

167
00:09:20,708 --> 00:09:23,583
que eran de estudiar, eran superútiles.

168
00:09:24,125 --> 00:09:27,417
Entonces, bueno,
me metí en esa compañía

169
00:09:28,167 --> 00:09:30,083
y me fui de gira.

170
00:09:31,667 --> 00:09:34,792
Y ahí hubo otro momento crítico
en mi vida,

171
00:09:35,458 --> 00:09:39,375
porque decidí que eso de casarme
y de irme a vivir...

172
00:09:39,458 --> 00:09:40,958
No tenía ningún sentido.

173
00:09:41,583 --> 00:09:43,042
Que el mundo era inmenso,

174
00:09:43,792 --> 00:09:46,167
que la vida estaba llena de retos,

175
00:09:47,000 --> 00:09:50,875
llena de lugares por conocer,
personas con las que compartir,

176
00:09:52,500 --> 00:09:54,750
y que significaba ser dueña de mi vida.

177
00:09:55,583 --> 00:09:59,250
Y si me quedaba en mi casa
con mi maravilloso novio

178
00:09:59,958 --> 00:10:01,667
aquello no iba a funcionar,

179
00:10:01,750 --> 00:10:04,583
porque era como incompatible,
de alguna manera.

180
00:10:04,667 --> 00:10:06,958
Yo quería seguir corriendo y andando.

181
00:10:07,042 --> 00:10:11,875
Así que, de alguna manera, eso marca
un punto de inflexión en mi existencia,

182
00:10:12,542 --> 00:10:13,792
y a partir de ahí

183
00:10:14,500 --> 00:10:17,458
tengo la suerte
de no haber dejado de trabajar

184
00:10:18,167 --> 00:10:19,917
más de seis meses en mi vida.

185
00:10:20,917 --> 00:10:25,625
Pensad que esto eran 20 o 21 años
y tengo 55,

186
00:10:26,042 --> 00:10:29,875
con lo cual, no tengo más
que un enorme agradecimiento

187
00:10:30,417 --> 00:10:33,917
al empujón de mi maestro cuando me dijo:
"Preséntate a esas pruebas".

188
00:10:34,458 --> 00:10:35,750
Y a ese novio que me dijo:

189
00:10:35,833 --> 00:10:38,458
"Existe la Real Escuela Superior
de Arte Dramático y Danza",

190
00:10:38,542 --> 00:10:40,125
sin saber lo que estaba haciendo.

191
00:10:41,417 --> 00:10:46,000
Y esto es un poco el origen
de por qué me dedico a esto.

192
00:10:46,500 --> 00:10:48,750
Nunca he dejado de hacerlo

193
00:10:49,958 --> 00:10:51,458
porque siempre es distinto,

194
00:10:52,292 --> 00:10:54,083
porque me ha enseñado tanto,

195
00:10:54,167 --> 00:10:57,958
aprendo tanto cada día
de las personas con las que trabajo,

196
00:10:58,042 --> 00:11:01,750
de la gente que se sienta delante
a ver una función,

197
00:11:02,792 --> 00:11:06,250
he conocido países, maneras de pensar,

198
00:11:07,667 --> 00:11:09,750
me ha abierto tanto la cabeza,

199
00:11:09,833 --> 00:11:12,333
me ha enseñado tanto,
que cada día sigue haciéndolo

200
00:11:12,417 --> 00:11:16,333
y por eso creo que no se me quitan
las ganas nunca

201
00:11:17,000 --> 00:11:20,292
y me sigue produciendo
una enorme emoción y un enorme vértigo.

202
00:11:20,375 --> 00:11:22,542
Con los años me da cada vez más miedo.

203
00:11:23,500 --> 00:11:26,625
Así que si alguien piensa que esto
con los años se va quitando,

204
00:11:26,708 --> 00:11:27,875
se equivoca.

205
00:11:27,958 --> 00:11:29,250
El miedo va en aumento,

206
00:11:29,333 --> 00:11:33,333
porque a mayor tiempo en esto
y a mayor experiencia,

207
00:11:33,417 --> 00:11:35,167
mayor responsabilidad.

208
00:11:35,250 --> 00:11:39,083
Antes hacías un personaje que salía,
decía buenas tardes y se iba.

209
00:11:39,167 --> 00:11:42,958
Ahora tienes un monólogo de 50 páginas.

210
00:11:43,500 --> 00:11:46,333
Con lo cual, la responsabilidad
va siendo cada vez mayor,

211
00:11:46,917 --> 00:11:49,042
y el miedo va en aumento.

212
00:11:49,125 --> 00:11:51,833
No sabes lo que la gente espera de ti,

213
00:11:51,917 --> 00:11:55,333
se espera a veces demasiado,
te crea una enorme inseguridad,

214
00:11:55,417 --> 00:11:57,500
pero aun así
me sigue haciendo tan feliz.

215
00:11:58,208 --> 00:12:02,208
Y el día que pierda el miedo,
pues lo dejaré,

216
00:12:02,292 --> 00:12:05,125
porque si no me da miedo
ya no me interesa.

217
00:12:05,208 --> 00:12:06,583
Sentiré que ya lo sé todo,

218
00:12:06,667 --> 00:12:09,042
y si lo sé todo no merezco
estar en esta profesión.

219
00:12:10,458 --> 00:12:13,250
Así que, bueno,
esta es un poco una introducción.

220
00:12:14,500 --> 00:12:15,833
Y a partir de este momento,

221
00:12:15,917 --> 00:12:19,500
pues si vosotros queréis
preguntarme cualquier cosa,

222
00:12:19,583 --> 00:12:21,417
estaré feliz de compartir.

223
00:12:21,500 --> 00:12:24,458
Esto es una charla, ¿eh?
Estamos conversando unos con otros.

224
00:12:26,167 --> 00:12:27,625
Hola, Blanca, soy Sandra.

225
00:12:27,708 --> 00:12:30,500
Soy actriz y soy profesora de teatro
en Cuarta Pared.

226
00:12:31,167 --> 00:12:34,875
Y, bueno, desde Cuarta damos también
actividades extraescolares

227
00:12:34,958 --> 00:12:36,167
en los colegios,

228
00:12:36,250 --> 00:12:40,375
y no pretendemos que los chavales sean
Blanca Portillo o Robert De Niro,

229
00:12:41,042 --> 00:12:45,875
pero bueno, lo hacemos porque creemos
que es importante para ellos

230
00:12:45,958 --> 00:12:48,500
y que les viene muy bien
a la hora de relacionarse.

231
00:12:49,333 --> 00:12:52,000
Mi pregunta es, desde tu experiencia,

232
00:12:52,083 --> 00:12:54,333
¿qué beneficios crees
que tiene el teatro

233
00:12:54,417 --> 00:12:57,000
en los niños y en las niñas
de nuestro país?

234
00:12:58,125 --> 00:13:00,125
Uf, muchísimas, estoy segura.

235
00:13:00,208 --> 00:13:03,500
De hecho, muchos países lo tienen
como asignatura obligatoria.

236
00:13:04,417 --> 00:13:05,417
Obligatoria.

237
00:13:06,042 --> 00:13:09,125
Es una cosa que todo el mundo
debería hacer alguna vez en la vida.

238
00:13:09,208 --> 00:13:11,583
Todo el mundo,
da igual la edad que tengas.

239
00:13:11,667 --> 00:13:14,250
Pero en la infancia, con los críos,

240
00:13:14,750 --> 00:13:20,542
es un momento difícil porque no tienen
herramientas para moverse en la vida.

241
00:13:20,625 --> 00:13:24,208
Yo he dado clases a niños y a niñas.

242
00:13:24,917 --> 00:13:26,583
Les faltan herramientas.

243
00:13:26,667 --> 00:13:27,917
Y hay muchos pudores,

244
00:13:28,000 --> 00:13:31,458
es un momento
en el que se enfrentan a lo exterior

245
00:13:32,000 --> 00:13:35,708
cuando tienen su mundo en casa,
más o menos cómodo.

246
00:13:36,208 --> 00:13:37,875
El teatro te permite, primero,

247
00:13:37,958 --> 00:13:40,792
entrar en contacto con los otros
de forma sincera.

248
00:13:41,375 --> 00:13:45,667
Esto es una cosa curiosa de matizar.

249
00:13:46,208 --> 00:13:47,667
Cuando tú estás en el cole,

250
00:13:48,833 --> 00:13:51,625
tú compartes lo que se puede compartir
en el colegio.

251
00:13:51,708 --> 00:13:53,000
Pero haciendo teatro,

252
00:13:53,083 --> 00:13:56,417
lo primero que tienes que compartir
es miedo, emoción.

253
00:13:57,000 --> 00:13:58,750
Vas a trabajar con tus emociones,

254
00:13:59,417 --> 00:14:01,500
con tu sentido del ridículo.

255
00:14:02,375 --> 00:14:04,333
A perder el sentido del ridículo.

256
00:14:04,958 --> 00:14:09,500
Todos intentamos ser lo más sensatos
y lo más correctos en la vida,

257
00:14:10,083 --> 00:14:12,125
hacer las cosas más o menos bien,

258
00:14:12,833 --> 00:14:16,250
no caernos cuando vamos andando,
no trabucarnos, no hacer...

259
00:14:16,958 --> 00:14:19,667
No pasa nada, el derecho al error,

260
00:14:19,750 --> 00:14:23,292
las enseñanzas teatrales
te lo permiten constantemente.

261
00:14:23,375 --> 00:14:27,250
De hecho, la base del teatro
es la equivocación.

262
00:14:27,333 --> 00:14:31,458
Para aprender hay que equivocarse
para poder hacerlo bien,

263
00:14:31,542 --> 00:14:35,875
el error, acierto, error,
investigar cómo poder hacerlo mejor.

264
00:14:35,958 --> 00:14:39,083
Con lo cual, se les abre la cabeza,
se les quita el miedo.

265
00:14:39,167 --> 00:14:42,500
Yo recuerdo que, dando clases,
había un niño que era,

266
00:14:42,583 --> 00:14:45,125
digamos el malote del grupo.

267
00:14:45,208 --> 00:14:47,000
Siempre hay roles que se van...

268
00:14:47,083 --> 00:14:51,042
Había un chavalín que era
como el más gallito de todos.

269
00:14:52,208 --> 00:14:54,500
Los otros le tenían un cierto miedo.

270
00:14:54,583 --> 00:14:57,292
Cuando él soltaba una broma,
todos se la reían.

271
00:14:57,375 --> 00:15:00,042
Entonces, yo decidí darle
el personaje más serio,

272
00:15:00,125 --> 00:15:03,542
el más sensible,
el que estaba más triste.

273
00:15:03,625 --> 00:15:05,625
Y descubrió, dentro de él,

274
00:15:05,708 --> 00:15:08,708
que eso no solamente le hacía
no perder autoridad

275
00:15:08,792 --> 00:15:10,083
dentro de sus compañeros,

276
00:15:10,167 --> 00:15:13,000
sino que les mostraba
a los demás una faceta

277
00:15:14,500 --> 00:15:16,708
que no sabía que tenía,

278
00:15:16,792 --> 00:15:19,667
y que hacía que los demás
le quisieran de verdad,

279
00:15:19,750 --> 00:15:21,375
o le admiraran de verdad.

280
00:15:21,458 --> 00:15:23,375
Porque el chaval se lo tomó muy en serio

281
00:15:23,458 --> 00:15:25,917
y empezó a trabajar
con mucha dedicación.

282
00:15:26,458 --> 00:15:29,417
Con lo cual,
empezó a ser líder de otra manera,

283
00:15:29,500 --> 00:15:32,875
de una manera mucho más honesta,
porque lloraba,

284
00:15:32,958 --> 00:15:35,458
porque era capaz de llorar
delante de sus amigos.

285
00:15:36,000 --> 00:15:40,000
Y eso fue como una carambola,
eso fue pasando a los demás.

286
00:15:40,500 --> 00:15:42,333
Bueno, en aquella ocasión,

287
00:15:43,625 --> 00:15:45,750
yo tuve un problema con los profesores

288
00:15:45,833 --> 00:15:49,042
porque los niños quisieron
dejar de dar todo tipo de clases,

289
00:15:49,125 --> 00:15:50,458
de cualquier otra actividad,

290
00:15:50,542 --> 00:15:53,000
porque solamente querían
dar las clases de teatro

291
00:15:53,083 --> 00:15:56,083
y los profesores me dijeron:
"Se está convirtiendo en un problema

292
00:15:56,167 --> 00:15:58,542
porque los papás quieren
que estudien otras cosas".

293
00:15:58,625 --> 00:16:01,417
En fin, les abre muchísimos caminos,
sobre todo en la mente.

294
00:16:02,083 --> 00:16:04,458
Y en su forma de relacionarse
con los otros,

295
00:16:04,542 --> 00:16:06,000
y perder el pudor.

296
00:16:07,750 --> 00:16:10,833
A veces dicen que los actores
somos los grandes mentirosos.

297
00:16:10,917 --> 00:16:12,750
Se dice que un actor miente.

298
00:16:12,833 --> 00:16:16,583
Y yo creo que es todo lo contrario,
somos las personas que menos mentimos.

299
00:16:17,375 --> 00:16:21,000
Yo creo que el ciudadano en general,
las personas en general,

300
00:16:21,083 --> 00:16:22,333
nos construimos personajes

301
00:16:22,417 --> 00:16:24,875
que muchas veces
no tienen nada de verdad.

302
00:16:24,958 --> 00:16:27,125
Nos hacemos los fuertes
cuando somos frágiles,

303
00:16:27,208 --> 00:16:30,208
nos hacemos los frágiles
cuando en realidad todo nos lo resbala,

304
00:16:30,292 --> 00:16:32,583
nos construimos un personaje
de cara afuera

305
00:16:33,250 --> 00:16:36,083
e intentamos ser coherentes
con ese personaje

306
00:16:36,167 --> 00:16:37,458
a lo largo de toda la vida.

307
00:16:37,917 --> 00:16:41,500
Sin embargo, los actores vivimos,
precisamente, con la máscara quitada,

308
00:16:42,167 --> 00:16:46,000
sacando de nosotros todo lo que a veces
no queremos ver que tenemos.

309
00:16:46,083 --> 00:16:50,542
Entonces, eso a los niños les ofrece
una posibilidad de verse de otra manera.

310
00:16:51,583 --> 00:16:53,625
Perder el sentido el ridículo.

311
00:16:53,708 --> 00:16:56,500
Hacemos muchísimas cosas,
o dejamos de hacerlas,

312
00:16:56,583 --> 00:16:58,917
porque nos da vergüenza,
porque nos da pudor.

313
00:16:59,000 --> 00:17:01,292
"Yo no voy a poder hacer esto".
¿Por qué no?

314
00:17:01,375 --> 00:17:05,583
Hay siempre un "¿Por qué no?",
y eso creo que es sanísimo.

315
00:17:05,667 --> 00:17:07,958
Y luego, por otro lado,
cuando haces teatro...

316
00:17:09,250 --> 00:17:12,167
Y yo esto se lo explicaba a ellos,
y eran bien pequeños, ¿eh?

317
00:17:12,917 --> 00:17:15,792
Hicimos "El sueño de una noche
de verano" de Shakespeare.

318
00:17:16,708 --> 00:17:20,250
Inevitablemente,
empiezas a hablar de mitología,

319
00:17:21,250 --> 00:17:25,000
a hablar de Shakespeare como autor,
no solamente teatral,

320
00:17:25,708 --> 00:17:27,375
empiezas a hablar de su época.

321
00:17:27,958 --> 00:17:32,542
Con lo cual, empiezan a aprender
un montón de cosas colaterales

322
00:17:32,625 --> 00:17:35,042
que tienen que ver
con la enseñanza general,

323
00:17:35,125 --> 00:17:38,917
pero que las ven a través de ellos,
a través de su propio cuerpo.

324
00:17:39,000 --> 00:17:42,875
Lo que representa Puck en la función,
que es una especie de duende,

325
00:17:43,458 --> 00:17:46,083
tiene su valor y su sentido
dentro de la historia

326
00:17:46,167 --> 00:17:47,458
y empiezan a entender.

327
00:17:47,542 --> 00:17:50,542
"¿Y esto dónde lo puedo aprender?
¿Y qué libros hay sobre esto?".

328
00:17:50,625 --> 00:17:54,875
Y se les despierta la curiosidad
de una manera increíble.

329
00:17:54,958 --> 00:17:58,375
Y luego empiezan a aprender
que, sin el otro, tú no eres nada,

330
00:17:59,000 --> 00:18:00,500
y eso también es importante.

331
00:18:00,583 --> 00:18:02,500
No se trata de ser el mejor,

332
00:18:02,583 --> 00:18:06,000
se trata de ser un buen eslabón fuerte
dentro de una cadena fuerte.

333
00:18:06,625 --> 00:18:08,375
Y se forma un equipo,

334
00:18:08,458 --> 00:18:11,125
se forma un grupo
donde todos ayudan a todos,

335
00:18:11,208 --> 00:18:13,292
y se eliminan rivalidades.

336
00:18:13,375 --> 00:18:16,333
Aunque siempre alguien dice:
"¿Y yo por qué tengo menos frases?

337
00:18:16,417 --> 00:18:18,042
Yo quiero tener más frases".

338
00:18:18,125 --> 00:18:20,375
Todos llevamos un protagonista dentro.

339
00:18:20,875 --> 00:18:23,875
Pero bueno, cuando se dan cuenta,
les vas dando responsabilidades

340
00:18:23,958 --> 00:18:29,208
y se dan cuenta de que no hace falta ser
el protagonista dentro de la función.

341
00:18:29,292 --> 00:18:32,125
Luego tienes mucho más trabajo
que hacer detrás también.

342
00:18:32,208 --> 00:18:34,375
Tú eres el que va a ayudar a este
cuando sale,

343
00:18:34,458 --> 00:18:37,417
tú te encargas del vestuario,
tú le ayudas...

344
00:18:37,500 --> 00:18:40,333
La sensación de trabajo en colaboración,
todos juntos,

345
00:18:40,417 --> 00:18:42,042
que eso es la base del teatro,

346
00:18:42,583 --> 00:18:44,375
es que les enseña una barbaridad.

347
00:18:44,458 --> 00:18:47,917
Yo, ya te digo, lo que sé es
que acabaron diciéndome:

348
00:18:48,000 --> 00:18:50,500
"Mira, no vengas más,
no quieren hacer más que esto".

349
00:18:51,542 --> 00:18:52,583
E hicieron todo.

350
00:18:52,667 --> 00:18:55,333
Hicieron ellos el vestuario, la música,
lo hicieron todo.

351
00:18:56,000 --> 00:18:59,458
Y era precioso ver cómo niñas
que no se atrevían a decir ni mu

352
00:19:00,792 --> 00:19:04,708
acabaron subidas al escenario
haciendo personajes maravillosos,

353
00:19:04,792 --> 00:19:06,292
y eso es bellísimo verlo.

354
00:19:07,833 --> 00:19:10,125
Hay un aspecto
que me parece muy importante

355
00:19:10,208 --> 00:19:12,625
que es el aprender a hablar en público

356
00:19:13,208 --> 00:19:15,542
y el saber transmitir las ideas.

357
00:19:16,875 --> 00:19:21,042
No sé si alguna vez has tenido
ese temor a hablar en público.

358
00:19:22,458 --> 00:19:25,000
Pero ¿qué le podrías decir
a un niño o a un joven

359
00:19:25,917 --> 00:19:27,958
que sí que tenga este temor?

360
00:19:28,042 --> 00:19:30,667
Lo de hablar en público
es una cosa muy particular.

361
00:19:31,750 --> 00:19:35,833
Tened en cuenta
que en el 99% de las ocasiones

362
00:19:35,917 --> 00:19:38,333
un actor no habla con su propia voz,

363
00:19:39,375 --> 00:19:41,125
habla a través de un personaje.

364
00:19:41,708 --> 00:19:43,667
Con lo cual,
yo sé lo que tengo que decir,

365
00:19:44,667 --> 00:19:46,333
ya me lo he aprendido.

366
00:19:46,417 --> 00:19:50,000
Y no lo digo yo, lo dice ella o él.

367
00:19:51,917 --> 00:19:54,250
Eso te quita la mitad del problema.

368
00:19:55,500 --> 00:19:58,000
Yo entiendo hablar en público
esto que hacemos ahora.

369
00:19:58,083 --> 00:20:01,708
Yo me enfrento a una serie de personas
que me están mirando

370
00:20:02,458 --> 00:20:07,000
y no tengo un guion escrito,
no sé lo que voy a decir,

371
00:20:07,083 --> 00:20:08,500
y soy yo hablando.

372
00:20:08,583 --> 00:20:10,750
Esta vez soy yo, no es un personaje.

373
00:20:11,458 --> 00:20:15,583
A mí esto hoy me ha producido
una enorme...

374
00:20:16,500 --> 00:20:18,958
...excitación y un miedo terrible.

375
00:20:19,042 --> 00:20:21,000
Yo estoy muy nerviosa, os lo he dicho.

376
00:20:21,083 --> 00:20:23,708
Que es lo primero que creo
que uno tiene que asumir

377
00:20:23,792 --> 00:20:25,708
cuando va a hablar en público.

378
00:20:25,792 --> 00:20:28,250
Pone nervioso,
¿a quién no le pone nervioso?

379
00:20:28,333 --> 00:20:30,458
Porque ninguno queremos
hacer el ridículo,

380
00:20:30,542 --> 00:20:32,500
si es que esto es lo de siempre, ¿no?

381
00:20:32,583 --> 00:20:35,833
Cuando en realidad no pasa nada,
el ridículo es una cosa muy relativa.

382
00:20:35,917 --> 00:20:37,500
Yo lo que intento...

383
00:20:37,583 --> 00:20:39,958
Es verdad que hablamos
con un texto que no nos pertenece,

384
00:20:40,042 --> 00:20:45,417
pero quieras que no,
hay 400 personas sentadas,

385
00:20:45,500 --> 00:20:46,500
así,

386
00:20:47,208 --> 00:20:48,792
esperando a ver qué dices.

387
00:20:50,292 --> 00:20:52,917
A quien no le ponga eso nervioso
es que es un demente.

388
00:20:54,000 --> 00:20:57,125
Hay que ser muy demente
para que eso no te ponga nervioso.

389
00:20:57,208 --> 00:20:59,792
Y creo que es un problema,
no de los chavales,

390
00:20:59,875 --> 00:21:02,042
creo que también un profesor...

391
00:21:02,875 --> 00:21:05,417
Uno llega a una clase el primer día,
me imagino,

392
00:21:06,042 --> 00:21:08,792
y tú ves a un número de personas ahí,
así.

393
00:21:09,667 --> 00:21:11,167
Y dices: "Hola, ¿qué tal?".

394
00:21:11,875 --> 00:21:14,292
Una cosa es que tengas
costumbre de hacerlo

395
00:21:14,375 --> 00:21:16,458
y otra cosa es que no dé miedo.

396
00:21:16,542 --> 00:21:18,167
Da miedo siempre,

397
00:21:18,250 --> 00:21:21,208
y esto es una cosa que a mí me parece
que hay que asumir.

398
00:21:21,583 --> 00:21:24,875
Cuando alguien tenga que hablar,
si tenéis que hacerlo alguna vez:

399
00:21:25,375 --> 00:21:27,917
"Hola, tengo miedo". No pasa nada.

400
00:21:28,583 --> 00:21:29,708
Por otro lado,

401
00:21:30,833 --> 00:21:34,042
es bueno saber que no pasa nada
si te equivocas,

402
00:21:34,125 --> 00:21:36,000
que no pasa nada si te quedas en blanco.

403
00:21:36,083 --> 00:21:38,667
Nadie se va a morir,
nadie ahí sentado va a hacer ¡pum!

404
00:21:39,333 --> 00:21:42,958
¿Sabes? No hay un peligro,
no hay un riesgo real.

405
00:21:43,500 --> 00:21:47,667
El único riesgo es tu propio miedo
a hacer el tonto o a hacer el ridículo,

406
00:21:48,208 --> 00:21:51,417
el nivel que tú te pones a ti mismo,
el listón.

407
00:21:52,792 --> 00:21:55,208
Creo que hay una cosa
que a veces nos cuesta pensar

408
00:21:55,292 --> 00:21:56,583
cuando hablamos en público,

409
00:21:56,667 --> 00:21:59,958
y es que la gente que está ahí
está dispuesta a escuchar.

410
00:22:00,875 --> 00:22:03,167
En un teatro, porque han pagado.

411
00:22:03,250 --> 00:22:05,500
No siempre la gente paga
para escucharte.

412
00:22:05,583 --> 00:22:08,000
A veces lo pienso
y es lo que más nerviosa me pone.

413
00:22:08,083 --> 00:22:09,792
Han pagado para escuchar.

414
00:22:09,875 --> 00:22:12,292
Con lo cual,
también tienen una disposición.

415
00:22:13,000 --> 00:22:15,333
Y no son una masa de gente,

416
00:22:15,833 --> 00:22:17,250
son individuos,

417
00:22:17,333 --> 00:22:20,667
son seres humanos con nombre y apellido
cada uno de ellos.

418
00:22:21,250 --> 00:22:23,292
Eso es otra cosa
que a veces se nos olvida.

419
00:22:23,375 --> 00:22:26,042
Hablar en público
es hablar a una masa de gente.

420
00:22:27,417 --> 00:22:31,333
Son personitas con sentimientos,
con sus nervios también,

421
00:22:31,417 --> 00:22:34,417
me imagino que hoy vosotros también,
quieras que no, hay algo de:

422
00:22:34,500 --> 00:22:38,417
"Bueno, vamos a ver, aquí estoy,
a ver qué nos cuenta esta mujer".

423
00:22:38,500 --> 00:22:43,208
También tú estás en una situación
no cómoda en el salón de tu casa.

424
00:22:43,792 --> 00:22:45,208
Con lo cual, cuando uno piensa

425
00:22:45,292 --> 00:22:48,083
que el otro está casi
en la misma situación que tú,

426
00:22:48,167 --> 00:22:51,333
empiezas a perder el miedo, a relajar.

427
00:22:51,875 --> 00:22:54,542
Evidentemente,
tienes que saber qué quieres contar.

428
00:22:55,833 --> 00:22:57,708
Yo ahora mismo no sé,

429
00:22:57,792 --> 00:23:00,292
porque voy viendo
a ver qué me preguntáis

430
00:23:00,375 --> 00:23:02,625
y voy armando un discurso
sobre la marcha.

431
00:23:03,167 --> 00:23:05,167
Pero bueno,
también eso te lo da la vida,

432
00:23:05,250 --> 00:23:06,792
y los años, y la experiencia,

433
00:23:06,875 --> 00:23:09,917
y tener de verdad ganas
de compartir algo.

434
00:23:10,000 --> 00:23:12,208
Eso es otra cosa
que te quita mucho el miedo,

435
00:23:12,958 --> 00:23:16,042
la idea de: "Quiero compartir
lo que tengo con vosotros".

436
00:23:16,792 --> 00:23:18,583
Estáis aquí para escuchar

437
00:23:18,667 --> 00:23:20,750
y yo estoy aquí
para daros todo lo que tenga,

438
00:23:21,417 --> 00:23:24,083
y me produce bienestar y placer hacerlo.

439
00:23:24,917 --> 00:23:26,708
Nuestro trabajo, el de los actores,

440
00:23:26,792 --> 00:23:28,833
sin vosotros, sin el espectador,
no existe.

441
00:23:29,417 --> 00:23:33,083
El trabajo de un profesor,
sin alumnos, no tiene sentido.

442
00:23:33,750 --> 00:23:37,458
Cualquiera que dé un discurso
tiene un auditorio,

443
00:23:37,542 --> 00:23:39,250
tiene gente que le está escuchando,

444
00:23:39,333 --> 00:23:43,000
una audiencia que está ahí,
pendiente de lo que vaya a decir.

445
00:23:43,500 --> 00:23:45,583
Nervios vas a tener, miedo vas a tener,

446
00:23:45,667 --> 00:23:49,542
pero eres un ser humano queriendo
compartir con otros seres humanos.

447
00:23:50,583 --> 00:23:52,333
Hay profesores aquí, ¿verdad?

448
00:23:52,833 --> 00:23:54,542
¿Tú eres profesora?
-Yo sí.

449
00:23:55,250 --> 00:23:57,125
¿Puedes venir un momento, por favor?

450
00:24:00,125 --> 00:24:03,083
Tú estás acostumbrada
a estar delante de gente.

451
00:24:03,167 --> 00:24:05,250
-Sí.
-¿Verdad? Y normalmente...

452
00:24:05,333 --> 00:24:11,125
Hombre, un profesor, a veces,
quienes les escuchan están obligados.

453
00:24:12,125 --> 00:24:13,917
No es que paguen por estar ahí.

454
00:24:15,208 --> 00:24:17,792
Pero, en general,
están porque tienen que estar

455
00:24:17,875 --> 00:24:20,375
y saben que deben hacerlo y quieren.

456
00:24:20,458 --> 00:24:24,833
Hay una diferencia, me imagino,
y dime tú si me equivoco.

457
00:24:26,083 --> 00:24:27,750
Es muy distinto ver una masa

458
00:24:29,167 --> 00:24:30,750
y pasar la vista

459
00:24:30,833 --> 00:24:33,208
que ir mirándolos uno a uno, ¿verdad?
-Sí, totalmente.

460
00:24:33,292 --> 00:24:35,625
Inténtalo, uno por uno,

461
00:24:36,333 --> 00:24:38,958
y fíjate en un pequeño detalle
de cada uno de ellos.

462
00:24:40,417 --> 00:24:42,458
Y todos tienen los ojos puestos en ti.

463
00:24:43,750 --> 00:24:45,417
No miran a otro lado, ¿no?
-No, no.

464
00:24:47,208 --> 00:24:48,708
-Esto es interesante.
-Mucho.

465
00:24:48,792 --> 00:24:50,625
-Están por ti.
-Bueno, por ti.

466
00:24:50,708 --> 00:24:53,042
-No, ahora te están mirando a ti.
-Bueno, también.

467
00:24:53,125 --> 00:24:54,583
Ahora te están mirando a ti.

468
00:24:55,250 --> 00:24:56,292
Y te miran.

469
00:24:57,458 --> 00:25:00,292
Y él, y el otro, y ella.

470
00:25:00,375 --> 00:25:02,917
Y ves que mueve un pie,
también está nerviosa, un poco.

471
00:25:04,375 --> 00:25:05,708
Vas mirándoles.

472
00:25:06,417 --> 00:25:08,583
Y se produce una conexión.
-Sí.

473
00:25:09,083 --> 00:25:10,667
Tú, cuando das clases,

474
00:25:10,750 --> 00:25:13,542
¿miras la clase entera
o les miras individualmente?

475
00:25:13,625 --> 00:25:15,958
-No, se mira individualmente.
-¿Verdad?

476
00:25:16,042 --> 00:25:18,417
Y eso hace que pierdas
un poquito el miedo.

477
00:25:18,500 --> 00:25:20,833
-Y que estén más contigo.
-Ah, amiga.

478
00:25:21,625 --> 00:25:24,083
Ese es uno de los grandes retos
de hablar en público:

479
00:25:24,167 --> 00:25:25,458
conseguir la atención.

480
00:25:26,583 --> 00:25:27,792
Captar.

481
00:25:27,875 --> 00:25:30,292
Y la única manera
de captar la atención es dar.

482
00:25:31,083 --> 00:25:31,958
Dar.

483
00:25:32,542 --> 00:25:34,958
Es un acto de generosidad.

484
00:25:35,458 --> 00:25:38,375
Y eso se nota mucho en los políticos.
¿No lo habéis notado,

485
00:25:38,917 --> 00:25:40,958
cuando un político
no habla para nosotros?

486
00:25:41,833 --> 00:25:45,000
Hace así, mete la mirada hacia adentro
y está hablando para él

487
00:25:45,917 --> 00:25:47,125
o para una masa.

488
00:25:47,625 --> 00:25:50,500
Cuando alguien deposita en ti la mirada,

489
00:25:51,250 --> 00:25:54,750
tú dices: "Ay, es para mí,
me está hablando a mí".

490
00:25:55,375 --> 00:25:58,708
Entonces, se establece vínculo
y hacen los nervios... ¡fum!

491
00:25:58,792 --> 00:25:59,792
-Sí.
-¿Verdad?

492
00:25:59,875 --> 00:26:01,333
-Un poquito.
-Mira qué mona.

493
00:26:01,833 --> 00:26:03,000
Gracias.
-A ti.

494
00:26:14,875 --> 00:26:17,375
Es hermoso porque es
un acto de generosidad.

495
00:26:18,125 --> 00:26:20,333
Hablar en público
es un acto de generosidad.

496
00:26:21,000 --> 00:26:22,792
"Tengo algo para daros".

497
00:26:22,875 --> 00:26:25,542
Y a partir de ese momento,
la gente se viene contigo.

498
00:26:25,625 --> 00:26:27,042
A no ser que digas una sandez.

499
00:26:28,625 --> 00:26:31,625
O una cosa a destiempo.

500
00:26:32,083 --> 00:26:33,375
Pero en general...

501
00:26:33,458 --> 00:26:36,458
Es más, yo lo he comprobado,
si tú le dices a la gente...

502
00:26:36,542 --> 00:26:39,458
En el teatro no puedes decirles:
"Hola, estoy muy nerviosa".

503
00:26:39,542 --> 00:26:41,375
Porque nadie te va a perdonar, ¿no?

504
00:26:41,875 --> 00:26:43,000
Nadie te lo va a perdonar.

505
00:26:43,083 --> 00:26:46,458
No puedes ponerles
en el programa de mano:

506
00:26:46,542 --> 00:26:48,500
"Me hubiera gustado ensayar
20 días más".

507
00:26:48,958 --> 00:26:53,083
No puedes. Pero hay algo de eso,
de comunicar, de comunicación.

508
00:26:53,167 --> 00:26:57,667
Es que nos creemos que hablar en público
es una cosa de un señor o una señora

509
00:26:57,750 --> 00:27:01,208
frente a otros que no existen
o que son una masa.

510
00:27:01,292 --> 00:27:05,708
No, son individuos, uno y otros unos,

511
00:27:06,542 --> 00:27:09,208
y que tienen su interés y su...

512
00:27:09,292 --> 00:27:11,292
Si ves que alguien de repente hace...

513
00:27:11,375 --> 00:27:14,750
"Ay, se me ha ido uno.
Voy a intentarlo, hay algo...".

514
00:27:14,833 --> 00:27:18,208
Claro que para hablar
delante de 5000 personas,

515
00:27:18,292 --> 00:27:20,750
yo que sé, o de 45.000,
pero en el fondo...

516
00:27:20,833 --> 00:27:23,833
Yo lo he hablado con gente del rock,
por ejemplo, con músicos,

517
00:27:24,625 --> 00:27:26,000
y es lo mismo.

518
00:27:26,083 --> 00:27:29,917
Te dicen: "Yo no veo una masa informe
de gente que canta a la vez,

519
00:27:30,000 --> 00:27:32,542
yo quiero ir al corazón de cada uno".

520
00:27:32,625 --> 00:27:34,625
O por lo menos esa es la intención.

521
00:27:34,708 --> 00:27:37,000
Y eso es lo que hace
que dejes de pensar en:

522
00:27:37,083 --> 00:27:40,292
"¿Estaré hablando bien? ¿Estaré mona?
¿Se me entenderá?

523
00:27:40,375 --> 00:27:42,458
¿He hecho bien tocándome la nariz?".

524
00:27:42,542 --> 00:27:45,708
Dejas de pensar en eso
y empiezas a comunicarte con el otro,

525
00:27:46,208 --> 00:27:47,292
a respirar

526
00:27:48,250 --> 00:27:53,208
y a ser un ser humano más
que tiene algo que compartir,

527
